title: Oncall handoff pulse and customer message canvas
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Summary:
This document defines a compact, repeatable oncall handoff 'pulse' protocol and an associated customer message canvas used for SLA-sensitive incidents. It is designed for frontline operators, incident commanders, and SREs to accelerate warm-handoffs, standardize what evidence to collect, and provide pre-approved customer status templates for each incident phase.

Scope and audience:
- Scope: all Redwood public and enterprise-facing inference services (hosted API, Dedicated routing, and Private control plane).
- Audience: oncall operators, bridge leads, SREs, support on-call, and customer success liaisons.

Why this exists:
- Handoffs are a high-risk time for information loss and slow restoration.
- Customers require consistent, SLA-aligned messaging.
- Engineers need a minimum set of evidence to triage and produce regulatory artifacts.

Key definitions:
1) Pulse: a 5-minute structured handoff exchange capturing state, evidence, and next actions.
2) Quiet window: a 10–30 minute period after a handoff where only critical changes are made; used to stabilize and prevent oscillation.
3) Evidence bundle: minimal artifacts required to validate severity and timeline for post-incident review.

Severity mapping (for pulse context):
- Sev-1: Full outage impacting >10% of customers or any enterprise SLA breach.
- Sev-2: Significant degradation (latency SLO degradation >50th percentile) or partial regional outage.
- Sev-3: Minor degradation or isolated tenant impact.

Pulse protocol (5-minute structured handoff):
1. Attest (30s): outgoing operator states: "I am handing off; current incident state: SEV-X; bridge open; primary hypothesis: <one-line>".
2. Evidence check (90s): outgoing lists evidence bundle items present (see Evidence collection table).
3. Actions and blockers (60s): outgoing reviews in-flight actions, who is owning them, and blockers.
4. Timeboxing and quiet window (30s): agree the next 15/30 minute quiet window and who will break it.
5. Acceptance (30s): incoming confirms understanding, repeats 1–2 critical next steps aloud, and declares a new heartbeat schedule.
6. Update status page & CSR (remaining time): outgoing or incoming (pre-agreed) posts the next public update.

Evidence collection (minimum required for SLO and postmortem):
- Requested artifacts (collect and attach to the incident ticket):
  * Time range (UTC) for observed deviation.
  * Aggregated 1m and 5m latency histograms for affected endpoints (csv).
  * Recent autoscaler events (timestamped).
  * Host / GPU node IDs and kube pod IDs (for Dedicated/private).
  * Model variant used (name + version + quantization profile).
  * Representative request/response sample (anonymized) showing failure or degradation.
  * Error traces (stack traces, grpc/HTTP codes), and cold start counts.
  * Any recent config/rollout IDs (canary id, rollout job id).

Evidence table (copy into incident ticket):
| field | why it matters | command / link |
|---|---|---|
|Time range|Bounds the incident window|N/A|
|Latency histograms|Proves SLO regression|curl https://observability/api/latency?s=...|
|Autoscaler events|Shows capacity churn|kubectl get events --namespace=inference|
|Node/pod IDs|Ties to infra failures|kubectl get pods -o wide --selector=...|
|Model variant|Identifies model-level regressions|cat /deploys/current_model.txt|
|Request sample|Reproduces customer impact|Extract via internal trace ID payload|

Note: paste the above as plain text in the ticket if attachments are delayed.

Status page and customer message canvas (SLA-sensitive templates):
- Template rules: keep messages factual, avoid speculation, and include: impact, affected region/tenants, mitigation steps underway, ETA or next update window, and a contact/CSR escalation path.

Initial acknowledgement (within 15 minutes for Sev-1, 30 minutes for Sev-2):
Subject: [Redwood] Incident — {service} {SEV-1/2} — {short summary}
Message body:
We are aware of an issue impacting {service}.
Impact: {brief, e.g. "Some API requests return 500 / Observed latency > 2s for <region>"}.
Customers affected: {public / list enterprise tenants when known}.
What we are doing: {brief bullet list of immediate mitigation actions}.
Next update: {T+15 / T+30 / promise window}.
Contact: {csr-email and status page link}.

Stabilization update (during quiet window):
Subject: [Redwood] Incident update — {service} — current state
Message body:
Summary of changes since last update. Attach evidence snapshot (latency percentile snapshot). If rollback or fallback executed, list rollout id and who initiated.

Post-incident status and customer reconciliation (within SLA window per contract):
Subject: [Redwood] Incident resolved — {service} — post-incident summary
Message body:
Root cause (as-of current understanding): {one-paragraph}.
Impact summary: total minutes degraded/outage, tenants affected, and credits (if applicable).
Evidence: attach evidence bundle (histograms, traces, and representative request/responses).
Next steps: remediation, follow-ups, and expected timeline for long-term fixes.

Handoff checklist (what the incoming must verify within first 10 minutes):
- Confirm bridge URL and ticket link is reachable.
- Confirm severity mapping and whether SLA credit process is triggered.
- Validate evidence bundle presence or initiate collection.
- Confirm owner for: model rollback, autoscaler tuning, routing policy change.
- Confirm customer comm schedule and who is authoring the public update.

Quiet-window rules and exceptions:
- Quiet window default: 15 minutes after each handoff for Sev-1, 10 minutes for Sev-2.
- Only break quiet window for: new evidence changing hypothesis, confirmed mitigation efficacy (rollback success/failure), or safety/regulatory requirement.
- Anyone breaking the quiet window must call 'breaking quiet' in the bridge and update ticket with reason.

Game day plan: Pulse Drill (30–60 minute exercise to validate handoffs):
Purpose: exercise the 5-minute pulse handoff under load with simulated evidence delays.
Roles:
- Incident conductor (1): runs timeline and injects faults.
- Bridge operators (2): outgoing and incoming.
- Customer comm (1): drafts and publishes status updates.
- Evidence steward (1): simulates delayed logs/attachments.
Scenario steps:
1. Inject simulated latency spike in Europe region.
2. Outgoing operator runs first pulse, collects partial evidence.
3. After 5 minutes, outgoing hands off per protocol; incoming performs acceptance.
4. Evidence steward releases delayed artifacts after 8 minutes; teams must update ticket.
5. Run through two handoffs and a forced quiet window break.
Success criteria:
- All handoffs completed within 5 minutes.
- Status page updated within required windows.
- Evidence bundle at least 80% complete by T+20.

Escalation and ownership matrix (quick reference):
- Oncall operator: first responder and ticket maintenance.
- Service steward (team owning service): technical ownership after stabilization.
- Bridge lead / incident commander: coordinates cross-team actions.
- Customer Success: external comms and SLA reconciliation.
- Security: loop in if data exposure is possible.

Post-incident artifacts and timeline for closure:
1. Incident ticket updated with final evidence bundle (within 48 hours).
2. Postmortem draft (blameless) created within 72 hours and assigned reviewers.
3. Remediation actions tracked as tasks with owners and target dates (linked in ticket).
4. SLA credit assessment completed and communicated per contract.

Appendix A — Quick copy-paste status templates:
- ACK template (Sev-1):
[ACK] We are investigating increased error rates in {service} in {region}. We will update within 15 minutes.

- UPDATE template (mid-incident):
[UPDATE] Mitigation applied: {action}. Observed effect: {latency P95 down from X to Y}. Next update: {T+30}.

- RESOLVE template:
[RESOLVED] The incident affecting {service} has been resolved. Root cause: {short}. Impact: {duration and tenants}. Full post-incident report: {link}.

Appendix B — Example CLI snippets for evidence extraction:
- Latency snapshot (example): curl -s "https://observability/api/latency?s=2026-03-01T12:00:00Z&e=2026-03-01T12:30:00Z&service=inference" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" > latency.csv
- Pod list for a rollout: kubectl get pods -n inference -l rollout=canary-2026-03 -o wide

Change log:
- 2025-11-12: Document created by Aisha Patel.
- 2026-03-02: Updated quiet-window defaults and added Pulse Drill game-day steps.

Ownership and training:
- Owner: SRE Ops (oncall-and-incident-response).
- Training: all oncall operators must complete Pulse Drill at least twice per 6 months.

Feedback and improvements:
- Send suggested edits or additional templates to the oncall playbook Slack channel (#oncall-playbook) or file changes as PRs to the runbook repository.
